docs.title: OrAC — Butler of the House
docs.text: Your home's dedicated butler bot. Monitors sensors, answers queries, and eventually speaks to you.

docs.title: What is OrAC?
docs.text: OrAC is a continuously-running butler bot that connects to your Home Assistant instance and acts as an intelligent layer on top of your smart home.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Status Climate monitoring (temp/humidity) ✅ Phase 1 Sensor auto-discovery ✅ Phase 1 Natural language queries ✅ Phase 1 REST API for on-demand access ✅ Phase 1 Alert system (battery, temp, humidity) ✅ Phase 1 Smart rules engine 🔜 Phase 2 Morning briefing 🔜 Phase 2 Voice interface (STT → LLM → TTS) 🔜 Phase 3 Context-aware learning 🔜 Phase 4

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install orac
orac init                    # Create config
orac start                   # Run the butler
orac query temp benjamin    # Ask a question

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: OrAC exposes a REST API on port 8901 (configurable).

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: http://localhost:8901

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Health check endpoint.

Response: 

{"health": "ok"}

docs.title: GET /status
docs.text:
Get OrAC status.

Response: 

{
  "status": "running",
  "sensors": 12,
  "pending_alerts": 0
}

docs.title: GET /sensors
docs.text:
List all registered sensors.

Response: 

{
  "sensors": [
    {
      "entity_id": "sensor.benjamin_temp",
      "friendly_name": "Benjamin's Bedroom",
      "device_class": "temperature",
      "value": 23.4,
      "temp": 23.4,
      "humidity": null,
      "battery": null,
      "updated": "2026-09-23T13:16:16+00:00"
    }
  ],
  "count": 12
}

docs.title: GET /temp
docs.text:
List all temperature sensors.

Response: 

{
  "temperature_sensors": [
    {
      "entity_id": "sensor.benjamin_temp",
      "friendly_name": "Benjamin's Bedroom",
      "temp": 23.4,
      "updated": "2026-09-23T13:16:16+00:00"
    }
  ],
  "count": 8
}

docs.title: GET /query?q=<query>
docs.text:
Natural language query.

Parameter Description Example q Query string temp benjamin

Response: 

{
  "query": "temp benjamin",
  "type": "temp_query",
  "data": [
    {
      "entity_id": "sensor.benjamin_temp",
      "friendly_name": "Benjamin's Bedroom",
      "temp": 23.4,
      "humidity": null,
      "updated": "2026-09-23T13:16:16+00:00"
    }
  ],
  "message": ""
}

Query Types:

  • temp_query — Temperature data
  • sensor_list — All sensors
  • battery_report — Battery status
  • status — OrAC status
  • error — Parse error

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Meaning 400 Bad request (missing q or parse error) 500 Internal server error

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: OrAC is built on a modular, event-driven architecture designed to run continuously on a dedicated machine.

docs.title: Engine (orac.engine)
docs.text:
The heart of OrAC. Manages the asyncio event loop and coordinates all subsystems.

  • start() — Initializes subsystems, connects to HA, starts polling
  • stop() — Graceful shutdown of all tasks
  • run() — Sync entry point with signal handling

docs.title: HA WebSocket Client (orac.core.ha_client)
docs.text:
Connects to Home Assistant via its WebSocket API (not HTTP polling).

  • connect() — WebSocket handshake + auth
  • get_current_states() — Fetch all entity states
  • subscribe_states() — Listen for state changes in real-time
  • discover_sensors() — Filter for temp/humidity/battery sensors
  • call_service() — Call HA services (TTS, notifications, etc.)

docs.title: Sensor Registry (orac.sensors.registry)
docs.text:
In-memory store of sensor snapshots with automatic discovery.

  • register() — Add a new sensor
  • update_from_states() — Bulk update from HA states
  • get_by_name() — Fuzzy search by friendly name
  • get_low_battery() — Filter sensors below threshold
  • get_history() — Time-windowed history

docs.title: Query Parser (orac.core.query)
docs.text:
Natural language to structured queries using regex patterns.

Supported patterns: - temp [name] → temperature query - humidity [name] → humidity query - battery → battery report - sensors → full sensor list - status → OrAC status

docs.title: Alert Manager (orac.alerts.alert_manager)
docs.text:
Monitors sensor values against configured thresholds.

Alert categories: - battery_low — Sensor battery below threshold - temp_high / temp_low — Temperature out of range - humidity_high / humidity_low — Humidity out of range

Features: - Deduplication (same alert won't re-fire) - Acknowledgment (clear specific alerts) - Multi-channel dispatch (push, TTS)

docs.title: REST API (orac.api.server)
docs.text:
aiohttp-based server on configurable port.

Route Method Purpose /health GET Health check /status GET OrAC status /sensors GET All sensors /temp GET Temperature sensors /query?q= GET Natural language query

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Discovery — On startup, HA client fetches all states and filters for temp/humidity/battery sensors
  2. Polling — Every monitoring.poll_interval seconds, engine fetches states and updates registry
  3. Alerting — After each poll, alert manager checks thresholds and dispatches notifications
  4. Query — CLI/API requests hit the query parser, which searches the registry and returns results
  5. Heartbeat — Every 10 minutes, logs sensor count and pending alert count

docs.title: Future Phases
docs.text: Phase Component Description 2 Rules Engine If/then rule expressions with built-in rules 2 Briefing Daily morning briefing via TTS/notify 3 Voice Wake word → STT → LLM → TTS pipeline 4 Learning Context-aware suggestions, routine learning

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: OrAC provides a command-line interface built with Click.

docs.title: orac init
docs.text:
Initialize configuration at ~/.config/orac/config.yaml.

orac init

Creates a default config with all available options documented.

docs.title: orac start
docs.text:
Start the butler engine. Runs indefinitely until stopped.

orac start
orac start --config /path/to/config.yaml

docs.title: orac query <query>
docs.text:
Query sensor data using natural language.

orac query temp benjamin
orac query temp
orac query humidity kitchen
orac query humidity
orac query sensors
orac query battery
orac query status

docs.title: orac --version
docs.text:
Display version information.

orac --version

docs.title: Query Syntax
docs.text: OrAC understands natural language patterns:

docs.title: Temperature Queries
docs.text: Pattern Example temp <name> orac query temp benjamin what's the temp orac query what's the temp temperature <name> orac query temperature living room

docs.title: Humidity Queries
docs.text: Pattern Example humidity <name> orac query humidity kitchen what's the humidity orac query what's the humidity

docs.title: Special Queries
docs.text: Pattern Description sensors List all registered sensors battery Check battery levels status Show OrAC status

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error (missing config, query failed)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: OrAC uses a YAML configuration file stored at ~/.config/orac/config.yaml.

docs.title: Initialize
docs.text: orac init

docs.title: Full Configuration Reference
docs.text:
home_assistant:
  url: "http://192.168.1.100:8123"     # Your HA instance URL
  access_token: ""                       # Long-lived access token

sensors:
  watch: []                            # Explicit sensor IDs (empty = auto-discover)
  alert_on_temp_high: 30               # °C threshold
  alert_on_temp_low: 10                # °C threshold
  alert_on_humidity_high: 70           # % threshold
  alert_on_humidity_low: 20            # % threshold
  alert_on_battery_low: 20             # % threshold

monitoring:
  poll_interval: 60                    # Seconds between sensor polls
  history_retention: 168               # Hours (7 days)

api:
  enabled: true                        # Enable REST API
  host: "0.0.0.0"                     # Bind address
  port: 8901                          # Port number

alerts:
  enabled: true
  notify_via:
    - "notify.iphone"                  # Home Assistant notification target
  tts_via:
    - "tts.google_translate_en_com"   # TTS engine
  media_player: "media_player.ta_an1000"  # Speaker for voice alerts

voice:
  enabled: false                       # Enable voice features
  wake_word_model: "porcupine"         # Wake word engine
  stt_model: "whisper_tiny"           # Speech-to-text model
  stt_engine: "local"                 # local | openai
  llm_model: ""                       # LLM API endpoint
  tts_engine: "ha_tts"                # Text-to-speech engine

logging:
  level: "INFO"                       # DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR

docs.title: Getting a Long-Lived Access Token
docs.text:
1. Open Home Assistant → Settings → People
  2. Click your user name
  3. Scroll to Long-Lived Access Tokens
  4. Generate a new token (name it "OrAC")
  5. Copy the token into config.yaml

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
The following environment variables can override config values:

Variable Overrides ORAC_HA_URL home_assistant.url ORAC_HA_TOKEN home_assistant.access_token ORAC_CONFIG_PATH Config file location

docs.title: Config Priority
docs.text:
1. Command-line flags (highest)
  2. Environment variables
  3. config.yaml
  4. Built-in defaults (lowest)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 5 (4GB or 8GB RAM)
  • Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (Bookworm)
  • Network access to Home Assistant

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
# Update system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install Python 3.13
sudo apt install -y python3.13 python3.13-venv python3.13-dev python3-pip

# Create OrAC user
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash orac

# Switch to orac user
sudo su - orac

# Clone and install
cd ~/projects
git clone https://github.com/your-org/orac.git
cd orac
python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .

# Initialize config
orac init
# Edit ~/.config/orac/config.yaml with your HA URL and token

# Test run
orac start
# Ctrl+C to stop

# Set up systemd service
sudo cp /home/orac/projects/orac/deploy/orac.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable orac
sudo systemctl start orac

docs.title: Service File
docs.text:
Create /home/orac/projects/orac/deploy/orac.service:

[Unit]
Description=OrAC Butler Bot
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=orac
Group=orac
WorkingDirectory=/home/orac/projects/orac
Environment=PATH=/home/orac/projects/orac/.venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
ExecStart=/home/orac/projects/orac/.venv/bin/orac start
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: Power Considerations
docs.text:
The Pi 5 is already very power-efficient. OrAC's memory footprint is minimal:

  • Idle: ~30 MB RAM
  • With 50 sensors: ~45 MB RAM
  • CPU: Near-zero when idle (polling interval)

docs.title: SD Card Longevity
docs.text:
OrAC writes no files to disk during normal operation. The only writes are:

  • Config file (written once during orac init)
  • Logs (controlled by logging.level in config)

Recommendation: Use a high-endurance SD card or USB SSD boot.

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text:
# Update system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install Python and deps
sudo apt install -y python3.13 python3.13-venv python3-pip

# Create OrAC user
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash orac

# Switch to orac user
sudo su - orac

# Clone and install
cd ~/projects
git clone <your-repo> orac
cd orac
python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .

orac init
# Edit ~/.config/orac/config.yaml with your HA URL and access token

docs.title: Systemd Service
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/orac.service:

[Unit]
Description=OrAC Butler Bot
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=orac
Group=orac
WorkingDirectory=/home/orac/projects/orac
Environment=PATH=/home/orac/projects/orac/.venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
ExecStart=/home/orac/projects/orac/.venv/bin/orac start
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable and start:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable orac
sudo systemctl start orac

# Check status
sudo systemctl status orac
journalctl -u orac -f

docs.title: Development Phases
docs.text: OrAC is being built in four phases, each adding significant capabilities.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Climate Monitor + Query Engine ✅
docs.text: Status: Complete. All 15 tests passing.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Config System — YAML config with defaults, ~/.config/orac/config.yaml
  • HA WebSocket Client — Connect, subscribe, discover sensors
  • Sensor Registry — Auto-discovery, snapshot management, history
  • Query Parser — Natural language parsing (temp, humidity, battery)
  • REST API — aiohttp server with /sensors, /query, /health
  • Alert Manager — Threshold monitoring with deduplication
  • CLI — Click-based interface with init, start, query commands

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
orac/
├── cli.py              # CLI commands
├── engine.py           # Main event loop
├── config/loader.py    # Config loading
├── core/
│   ├── ha_client.py    # HA websocket client
│   └── query.py        # Query parser
├── sensors/registry.py # Sensor registry
├── alerts/alert_manager.py
└── api/server.py       # REST API

docs.title: Planned Components
docs.text:
• Rule Expression Parser — DSL for if/then/else rules
  • Built-in Rules
  • Solar peak → charge battery
  • Rain detected → close blinds
  • Daily briefing → TTS announcement
  • Anomaly detection → alert on unusual patterns
  • Morning Briefing — Weather + energy + presence summary

docs.title: Config Format
docs.text:
rules:
  - name: "solar_charge"
    condition: "solar_production > 5.0 kW AND battery_soc < 90"
    action: "set_charge_rate(max)"
  - name: "rain_blinds"
    condition: "weather.forecast_home.precipitation > 1"
    action: "close_cover.living_room"

docs.title: Planned Components
docs.text:
• Wake Word Detection — Porcupine/Picovoice local wake word
  • Speech-to-Text — Whisper (local) or OpenAI API
  • Intent Parser — LLM-based intent extraction
  • Text-to-Speech — HA TTS or local engine

docs.title: Voice Flow
docs.text: Audio Input → Wake Word → STT → LLM → Intent → Action → TTS → Audio Output

docs.title: Planned Components
docs.text:
• Context-Aware Suggestions — "It's getting dark, want me to turn on the lights?"
  • Routine Learning — Learn patterns over time
  • Personalization — Adapt to user preferences
